Space and defense news, Wed Oct 28

Top stories: the US picked Poland to host Europe's first PAC-3 Patriot interceptor maintenance hub, and the DIA says China's satellite fleet has tripled since 2018. Also, the UK, Netherlands, Finland and Poland are starting treaty talks on a joint defense procurement mechanism after the UK decided not to join Canada's defense bank.

NATO

  • The Pentagon chose Poland over Germany, the Netherlands and Norway for a PAC-3 repair and recertification facility worth about $253M. Germany, the Netherlands and Sweden will supply it, and it should open in about a year. Breaking Defense · Stars and Stripes
  • NATO's Communications and Information Agency, which buys the alliance's IT systems, wants ready-made missile defense battle management software, with first capability in 2028. Inside Defense
  • The UK, Netherlands, Finland and Poland are opening treaty talks on the Multilateral Defence Mechanism, which pools allied demand so countries can buy jointly. They aim to have it running in 2027. GOV.UK
  • The leaders of Finland and Norway held a call with Putin, a rare break in the freeze on contact since 2022. Breaking Defense
  • Finland's defense minister spoke about NATO, Ukraine and Russia. Defense News
  • At the E5 defense ministers' meeting in Paris, NATO's deputy chief said air defense keeps reaching Ukraine through PURL, NATO's program for buying US weapons for Ukraine. NATO
  • A drone attack hit a container ship off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast. AP News

EU and European defense

  • The European Commission is preparing a second round of SAFE, its EU defense loan program, worth about €21B for joint projects with Ukraine. 2eu.brussels
  • Britain won't join the Canada-led Defence, Security and Resilience Bank Defense News and is pushing its own European procurement scheme instead. Politico Europe
  • EU members are still split on calling Canada an "associate member," with the Montreal summit two days away. Politico Europe
  • Germany has to decide whether to join an existing fighter jet program or start its own. Politico Europe
  • UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting heads to Berlin for talks with his German counterpart, Boris Pistorius. Politico Europe
  • India says demand from ReArm Europe, the EU's defense spending plan, is boosting its ammunition exports to Europe. Defense News

United States

  • The DIA's space threat report says China's satellite fleet has tripled since 2018. Breaking Defense
  • The Pentagon plans a $150M loan to Stoke Space for a second launch pad at Cape Canaveral. Air & Space Forces
  • The Air Force awarded Lockheed Martin a $694M production contract for the ARRW hypersonic missile. Defense News
  • Castelion won an Air Force contract to put its Blackbeard hypersonic missile on the F-16. Air & Space Forces
  • Boeing's CEO is upbeat on defense after winning the F/A-XX fighter contract and says the company will avoid fixed-price deals. Air & Space Forces
  • SpaceX reportedly gets access to parts of Space Command's orbital tracking catalog in exchange for data from its own tracking system, Stargaze. The Space Force says that data is controlled but not classified. Science Times
  • Anduril and Qualcomm launched BlueChip, a computer line that includes laptops for government and military buyers. DefenseScoop
  • A Falcon 9 launched 27 Starlink satellites from Vandenberg on Oct 27, SpaceX's 117th Falcon 9 launch this year. Space.com

European space

  • ESA ordered four more second-generation Galileo navigation satellites from Thales Alenia Space and Airbus, bringing that fleet to 16. ESA
  • The planned "Bromo" merger of the Airbus, Thales and Leonardo satellite businesses faces EU antitrust doubts tied to IRIS², the EU's planned satellite constellation, and may face a lawsuit from OHB. A formal review may not start until early 2027. heise
  • ESA's Hera probe imaged the asteroids Didymos and Dimorphos as two separate objects for the first time. ESA
  • A Ukrainian startup and Denmark's GomSpace are testing a satellite that could lead to a Ukrainian-controlled communications network. SpaceNews

Global

  • China launched its 28th batch of low-orbit internet satellites from Hainan on Oct 25. Xinhua
  • The US Army is looking at high-altitude balloons to spot and hit targets along the first island chain, the arc of islands off China's coast. Defense News
  • Astroscale proposed fleets of "bodyguard" spacecraft to protect satellites from attacks in orbit. Space.com
  • There was nothing new on Golden Dome or on Congress and the defense budget today. I couldn't check Euractiv because the site blocked my access.
